inputs.original_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has made it harder to revoke pre-arrest bail, insisting on clear proof that someone misused their liberty or that circumstances changed—even when stolen articles are still missing and the allegations are serious. Justice Sumeet Goel dismissed the plea to cancel bail in a house case. That’s presented as a safeguard, but the effect is a ready-made shield: make the public prove what may be kept out of sight, then claim the rules were followed while the accused stays protected.
inputs.modified_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has made it harder to revoke pre-arrest bail, requiring clear proof that someone misused their liberty or that circumstances changed, even when stolen articles remain missing and the allegations are serious. Justice Sumeet Goel dismissed the plea to cancel bail in a house case. It is presented as a safeguard, but its effect is a ready-made shield: the public must prove what may be kept out of sight, while the accused stays protected under rules that are said to have been followed.
